name: Joiada
overview: Joiada was a male Levite known primarily as the son of Eliashib, as recorded in Nehemiah 12:10. His identity is closely tied to his priestly lineage within the tribe of Levi. Beyond this familial connection, the biblical record offers limited additional details about his life or ministry.
namesAndTitles: The name Joiada means 'YHWH knows,' reflecting a theologically rich meaning tied to God's knowledge and sovereignty. This proper name, referenced in Nehemiah 12:10, highlights a common biblical practice of embedding divine attributes within personal names.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Joiada as the son of Eliashib (Nehemiah 12:10) and the father of Jonathan (Nehemiah 12:11). These explicit relationships situate him within a priestly family line, emphasizing his role in the continuity of Levitical service.
scriptureSignificance: Joiada's significance lies in his place within the priestly genealogy recorded in Nehemiah, which underscores the restoration and leadership of the Levitical priesthood after the Babylonian exile. His mention as the son of Eliashib and father of Jonathan connects him to the ongoing spiritual leadership vital to Israel's worship and community life during the post-exilic period.
